subsystems: rendering - camera nudge and impulse flag
summary: One focused behavior: the section 48 distant-motion impulse — a distant large motion (creature or environmental) produces a low-amplitude, short-decay camera nudge and sets a presentation flag for the trigger duration that WI-06d-c's shake path will gate on. Trigger, nudge and flag are one impulse event, not shippable behaviors, tested together. Independently counted: 1 behavior, 3 changed responsibilities (Renderer.follow nudge offset; new small presentation-state flag module owning the set/decay/clear state; pure-data trigger params module) — at the three-responsibility limit, tests excluded per spec. Scope inventory verified against source: src/render/Renderer.ts follow() exists with the ~0.15s exponential lag (CAMERA_LAG_SEC) and bounds-clamping the spec says must stay untouched, so the nudge offset has a clean seam and no hidden owner. Dependencies are correct: [WI-06a, WI-06b, WI-06c] are parallel-generation siblings (inherited from the story), not ancestors (WI-06d-b/WI-06d) or descendants; no dependency on WI-06d-c is needed because b4 only produces the flag and WI-06d-c-a declares its own dependency on b4 for the flag->shake integration proof. Criteria: AC-art-geometry retained verbatim from the parent; AC-juice-impulse is a child-local criterion as documented in the story plan; the story-level union covers both parent criteria and the AC-art-geometry six-effect browser union has a named final proof owner (WI-06d-b6), which this leaf explicitly does not re-assert. Boundaries checked against both neighboring plans and consistent: the low-frequency gate, amplitude budget and the master shake flag (WI-06g's seam) are WI-06d-c's (c-a's) scope; the reduced-flashing suppression is only a design constraint (single-boolean suppressible), not an implementation here; particles, lighting, HUD and schools are named non-goals. Evidence is focused: Node unit tests for trigger params (distance band / motion threshold boundaries) and flag transitions (set on distant large motion, cleared after decay, not set by near or small motion), plus a local browser clip/screenshot of the nudge. Assumptions recorded: the flag module location (src/render/ vs src/game/) is left to the implementer and both are acceptable; the trigger evaluation (comparing observed motion/distance against the params) lives inside the flag/presentation-state module, keeping the owner count at three. A fresh implementer can proceed from the handoff (story plan, WI-06d-c, Renderer.ts, request sections 14.3, 16, 34, 35, 48, 70) without reconstructing the task.
